_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC BOS. Overlaid onto the schema built from BosConfig (a SosFadeConfig superset). UI ONLY — never touches a trade decision or the source hash. Click Scan Strategies after editing. THE CONTRACT: `label` is the Pine input's TITLE and `desc` is its TOOLTIP, both verbatim from indicators/mpc_bos_strategy.pine, changed in the same commit — one parameter, one name, one explanation, two UIs. They were EXTRACTED from the Pine by script rather than retyped, because a lab row saying something different from the chart is how a rule gets read backwards (exec_deep_fib said 'ABOVE' where its own tooltip said 'shallower', and that was false half the time). Params not listed here fall back to their raw field names; the inherited A+ fields that this fork pins are deliberately absent, because none of them is an input in this fork's Pine — see config.py for why each is pinned.
edge: A shift of structure tells you the trend has turned; what comes after it is where the money is. The market prints one or more BREAK OF STRUCTURE events in that same direction until another SOS ends the run, and each BOS is a fresh continuation leg giving a retracement you can buy or sell into. A+ fades the shift; this rides what the shift started. Not every BOS is real — some are the last poke before the reversal — so it is deliberately a FILTERED setup. At the 2026-08-07 defaults: every BOS in the regime arms a leg, a limit rests at fib 0.786 of that leg's retrace, the stop is 1.3x ATR, price must be closing on the trend's own side of the session VWAP, and the whole position leaves at TP3. NOT PARITY-VALIDATED — no compare_bos.py run has ever been green, so read the direction of any result here and never the decimals.

steps.label: 01 · SOS
steps.title: A shift opens a regime
steps.detail: A shift of structure fires and opens a regime on that side. Until it does, no break can arm — at the start of history the engine seeds a direction with no SOS behind it, and those seeded breaks never trade.

steps.label: 02 · BOS
steps.title: A continuation break arms a leg
steps.detail: Each later break of structure in the regime's direction is a fresh continuation leg. The newest break always owns the setup: an older armed leg is dropped the moment a new one prints, even if filters then refuse the new one.

steps.label: 03 · Retrace
steps.title: A limit rests in the band
steps.detail: A limit rests at the chosen fib of that leg's retracement (0.786 by default) and the tap IS the entry — no bar has to close inside the band. The leg dies if price completes the cycle, closes past the leg origin, or the day cap expires first.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Out at TP3 or at the ratcheting stop
steps.detail: Touching TP1 moves the stop to breakeven and TP2 lifts it to the floor, whatever the rung sizes are. At the shipped 0/0/100 nothing is banked early: the whole position leaves at TP3 (the leg extreme) or at the stop that has been ratcheting up behind it.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Take long setups. Off = the long side never arms, and every ready long setup is tagged blocked with 'Direction off' so you can still count what it cost.
params._desc_note: No tooltip on the Pine input — written here. Copy it back to the Pine before treating it as the shared text.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Take short setups. Off = the short side never arms, and every ready short setup is tagged blocked with 'Direction off'.
params._desc_note: No tooltip on the Pine input — written here. Copy it back to the Pine before treating it as the shared text.

params.name: bos_which
params.label: Which break after the shift
params.desc: The 1st break after a shift of structure is the EXPANSION; the 2nd and later are CONTINUATIONS. Default 'All' since 2026-08-07 — it was '1st only', and taking every break measured better at the 0.786 entry depth (see docs/MPC_BOS_OPTIMIZATION.md). Every trade's label records which number it was, so you can read off the chart whether the later ones were worth taking. ⚠ A 2nd break still CANCELS a 1st-break setup that is still waiting for its pullback — the newest break always owns the leg.

params.name: bos_min_disp_atr
params.label: Break must clear the swing by (x ATR)
params.desc: How far the breaking candle must CLOSE past the swing it broke, measured in ATR. A one-tick poke through a high is a liquidity grab, not a break. 0 = accept any break. Try 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 and compare.

params.name: bos_min_leg_atr
params.label: Break leg must be at least (x ATR)
params.desc: Minimum size of the break leg. A tiny leg's entry band is inside the noise — the stop is too tight to survive and the targets are inside the spread. 0 = no minimum.

params.name: bos_max_days
params.label: Drop an armed break after (days)
params.desc: How long an armed break waits for its pullback before the setup is dropped. Counted in bars rather than clock time, so weekends and the daily close don't use it up.

params.name: bos_max_per_regime
params.label: Max trades between shifts
params.desc: Stop taking new trades after this many fills since the last shift of structure, until the next shift. 10 = effectively off. Lower it to 2 or 3 to stop the strategy stacking losses into one choppy run.

params.name: bos_req_hold
params.label: Broken level must hold
params.desc: ON = a candle CLOSING back through the broken swing kills the setup. ⚠ This fights the entry as currently set: the 0.5-0.886 band sits BELOW the broken swing on most legs, so price normally has to close back through that level to reach your limit at all. With it on, the setup usually dies a few bars before its own order would have filled. Only coherent alongside a much shallower entry.

params.name: bos_fib_anchor
params.label: Measure levels on
params.desc: Which leg the entry band, the stop and the targets are measured on. 'Expansion leg' = from the leg's origin to the high it is still making, so the levels keep moving until the pullback confirms. 'Break leg' = frozen at the moment of the break. On a leg that ran a long way past the level it broke, these two sit far apart. ⚠ DEFAULT CHANGED TO 'Break leg' 2026-08-07, and the reason is honesty rather than a measured win: every number behind today's defaults was produced by a skeleton that FROZE the leg at the break bar, so 'Break leg' is the anchor those results actually describe. Running 'Expansion leg' means the entry depth, the stop and all three targets sit somewhere the measurement never looked. It has NOT been measured head-to-head — if you test it and Expansion wins, that is a real finding and the default should move back.

params.name: bos_entry_top
params.label: Shallowest the entry may rest
params.desc: The SHALLOW end of the entry band — how little of a pullback the strategy will accept. Default 0.5 = the band is 0.5-0.886 and nothing may rest above it; a gap sitting between 0.382 and 0.5 is pushed down to 0.5 or ignored. Set 0.382 to open the band to 0.382-0.886, so a gap in that shallower pocket prices the entry at its own edge. ⚠ Shallow entries fill far more often and pay far less per trade: with the default Fib 1.0 stop, a 0.382 entry risks ~0.62 of the leg to make ~0.15 to TP1 — under 0.25R — so the whole ladder compresses and only the runner earns. The deep end (0.886) does not move. NOT MEASURED — this is a lever to test, not a tuned value.

params.name: bos_use_fvg
params.label: Price the entry off a gap
params.desc: ON = the limit is placed on a fair value gap (or the Sniper Zone) inside the entry band — the gap the break left behind IS the entry. OFF (default since 2026-08-07) = a plain fib limit at the level below, and the five settings under this one grey out. ⚠ THIS DEFAULTED ON UNTIL 2026-08-07 AND IT WAS THE LOSING HALF OF THE BOOK. Two independent measurements say so: the 2026-07-31 Python sweep found the FVG entry was 98 trades for −15.1R with no tail at all (nothing bigger than +3.3R) while the rest of the book broke even, and the 2026-08-06 engine study found a plain 0.786 fib beats it by +14.5% over a matched random control where the gap-priced 0.5 band manages +3.7%. The mechanism is that the GAP decides where the limit rests, and it rests too shallow — see docs/MPC_BOS_OPTIMIZATION.md.

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: ↳ ...and require one (no gap = no trade)
params.desc: ON = if no gap qualifies, the setup does not trade at all. OFF = it still trades, at the fallback fib further down. Note the Sniper Zone counts as a gap here, so a leg that has a zone is not refused.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: ↳ ...gap must sit fully past the shallow end
params.desc: ON = the WHOLE gap has to be on the deep side of the band's shallow end (the level set above — 0.5 by default, 0.382 if you opened the band). OFF = a gap lying across that line also qualifies. Deeper entries are better prices but get reached less often.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: ↳ ...deep gap enters at the nearest fib
params.desc: For a gap sitting deeper than 0.618: rest the limit at the nearest fib just SHALLOWER than the gap — the price you reach first — instead of chasing the gap's own edge, which price may never tap.

params.name: exec_conf_sz2
params.label: ↳ ...Sniper Zone counts as a gap
params.desc: Lets the Sniper Zone (the 0.382-0.5 pocket of the break leg) price a leg that had no qualifying gap. OFF = a real gap is strictly required. The zone can stand in for a gap; it is never something the trade waits for.

params.name: exec_fvg_50
params.label: ↳ ...gap across the shallow end enters at it
params.desc: Last-resort entry: a gap lying ACROSS the band's shallow end (0.5, or 0.382 if you opened the band) rests the limit exactly AT that line. Ranked below every other source, so it only ever prices a leg nothing better could.

params.name: bos_entry_fib
params.label: Fallback entry level
params.desc: The plain limit price the trade rests at. ⚠ SINCE 2026-08-07 THIS IS THE PRIMARY ENTRY, NOT A FALLBACK — 'Price the entry off a gap' now defaults OFF, so this level is what actually gets traded. The name is kept because the setting is unchanged; only its default and its importance moved. 0.786 measured +14.5% over a matched random control (+4.1σ, 201 trades, 9 of 9 years positive) against +3.7% for the old 0.5-band gap entry. ⚠ DEPTH IS THE BIGGER LEVER THAN THE VWAP FILTER and the two compound. ⚠ Do NOT pair a deep entry with a tighter stop model: 0.786 against a 0.886 stop scored higher on paper and is a trap — its median stop is $0.74, so the spread alone eats 30% of R, and the deepest tenth of those trades have stops under $0.31. Keep the stop on 'Fib 1.0 (leg origin)'. Clamped by 'Shallowest the entry may rest' above: picking 0.382 while that is set to 0.5 just gives you 0.5.

params.name: bos_respect_veto
params.label: Divergence blocks a new entry
params.desc: ON = a long will not open while a bearish divergence is live or RSI is extremely overbought, and the mirror for shorts. Re-checked on every bar, so a divergence appearing while the setup waits PULLS the resting order; if it goes stale the order can be placed again. For a continuation trade an opposing divergence is the fakeout signature.

params.name: bos_vwap_req
params.label: Session VWAP filter
params.desc: Refuse a setup while price is not closing on the trend's own side of the session VWAP — above it for a long, below for a short. A STATE, not a cross: it never asks whether price crossed the line, only which side of it the bar closed. MEASURED 2026-08-06 on 186,384 real M15 bars: it roughly doubles this trigger's edge over a matched random control (+4.4% -> +6.8%) and cuts the median stop distance 38% (1.80 -> 1.11 ATR), which is the half that matters more, because a tighter stop is more size per unit of risk. ⚠ That measurement was taken on a SKELETON of this setup — a with-trend BOS retraced to 0.5, stop at 0.886 — not on this file's FVG entry, so treat it as a strong prior and not as this strategy's own number. Set 'Off' to reproduce anything measured before the filter existed.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-18:00 NY)
params.desc: Blocks NEW entries in the last hour before the daily close. Gold closes 17:00 New York and reopens 18:00, so this avoids trades that get gapped out over the break. A market-hours fact rather than a strategy opinion.

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias requirement
params.desc: Judged against the trade direction. Ignore = off. Must agree = the weekly has to match the trade. Must not oppose = neutral passes, only an opposing weekly blocks. For a continuation setup 'Must agree' is the natural one to try.

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias requirement
params.desc: Same four choices as Weekly, judged against the trade direction. Ignore = off.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: Percent of account equity risked per trade. Position size is worked out from this and the stop distance, so a wider stop automatically buys a smaller position.

params.name: bos_sl_model
params.label: Stop model
params.desc: Where the stop sits, before the buffer. 'Fib 1.0' = the origin of the leg, the widest and the level the engine itself uses to call the leg dead. 'Fib 0.886' and 'Last confirmed swing' are tighter. 'ATR' is a fixed distance from the entry. ⚠ 'Broken swing level' rarely works: for a long that level sits ABOVE the entry, which is not a stop, so almost every order is refused. Note a tighter stop pushes TP1 further away in R, and TP1 is what moves the stop to breakeven — so tighter protection arrives LATER, not sooner. ⚠ DEFAULT CHANGED TO 'ATR' 2026-08-07 AND IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE IMPROVEMENT MEASURED ON THIS STRATEGY. A fib stop is a FRACTION OF THE LEG (fib 1.0 at a 0.786 entry risks 0.214 of it), so a small leg produces a small stop MECHANICALLY — measured over 186,384 M15 bars the fib default's median stop is $1.58 and its tightest tenth is $0.64, where the $0.22 spread is 34% of R and a 15-minute bar's low cannot tell you whether the stop was touched at all. An ATR stop does not care how big the leg was: median $3.89, tightest tenth $2.06. Compared at a MATCHED 25% drawdown budget over 40 jittered replays, ATR beat the old fib default on 32 of 40, and cleared 4x on BOTH halves of the history in 28 of 40 against the fib default's 4 of 40. See docs/MPC_BOS_OPTIMIZATION.md → Run 7.

params.name: bos_sl_atr
params.label: ↳ ATR multiple
params.desc: Only used when the stop model above is 'ATR'. The stop sits this many ATR from the entry price. ⚠ 1.3 SITS ON A PLATEAU, NOT A PEAK, and that is the only reason it is defensible: measured at a matched 25% drawdown budget, 1.0 → 24.4x, 1.1 → 40.0x, 1.2 → 60.9x, 1.3 → 65.4x, 1.4 → 47.4x, 1.5 → 55.2x, 1.6 → 35.2x. Anything from 1.2 to 1.5 is the same answer inside the noise — the jitter audit puts run-to-run spread on this metric at roughly a factor of two, so do not read 65.4 against 55.2 as a difference. Below 1.0 the stop starts landing inside the spread again, which is the hazard the ATR model exists to remove.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Extra room beyond the stop (ticks)
params.desc: Pushes the stop this many ticks further away than the level chosen above, so a wick through the level doesn't take you out.

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Refuse a setup whose stop lands too close to the entry. This matters more than it looks: size is risk divided by stop distance, so a stop that collapses onto the entry does not risk less — it buys an enormous position that ordinary noise runs straight through. '% of price' keeps scaling as gold rises. Off greys out the floor below. ⚠ DEFAULT CHANGED TO '% of price' 2026-08-07, and it is a SECOND line of defence rather than the main one — with the ATR stop model above it only refuses about 7 setups in 168, because an ATR stop is already wide. It is on because the two failures it guards are silent: a stop inside the spread is not a small loss, it is an enormous position, and a backtest cannot even tell you it was hit. ⚠ It is NOT free to switch the stop model back to a fib without this: at 'Fib 1.0' this floor cuts the book from 168 trades to 55.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: ↳ Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: A PERCENT in '% of price' mode, DOLLARS of price in 'Fixed $', a MULTIPLE in 'x ATR(14)'.

params.name: bos_move_stop
params.label: Moving stop (trails from entry)
params.desc: A trail that runs from the moment you are FILLED, instead of waiting for TP2 like the runner trail in section 7. It follows the best price the trade has seen and can only ever pull the stop TIGHTER — it never loosens breakeven or the TP2 floor, and the two can run together. Off = the stop stays put until TP1 moves it to breakeven. ⚠ It only starts on the bar AFTER the fill: on the fill bar itself the high-water mark is the whole bar's high, including the move the position was never in, so trailing off it would stage a stop out of thin air.

params.name: bos_move_stop_val
params.label: ↳ trail distance (unit = mode above)
params.desc: How far the moving stop sits behind the best price seen. DOLLARS of price in '$ of price' (on gold 1 pip = $0.10, so 5.0 = 50 pips), and TICKS behind the last confirmed swing in 'Structure (swing)'. Too tight and normal noise scratches every trade before it can work — start wide and walk it in.

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the TP1 limit banks. ⚠ DEFAULT 0 SINCE 2026-08-07 — it was 30, and banking here MEASURED WORSE. Touching TP1 still moves the stop to breakeven whatever this is set to, so 0 keeps the protection and gives up only the partial. At the shipped 0.786 entry TP1 sits at ~1.34R, and taking a third of the position off there costs more than it saves: 30/30/20 scored +90.8R against 0/0/100's +137.7R on the same 171 trades. See docs/MPC_BOS_OPTIMIZATION.md → Run 6.

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the TP2 limit banks. ⚠ DEFAULT 0 SINCE 2026-08-07, same reason as TP1. Touching TP2 still lifts the stop to the floor set in section 7 and hands the rest to the trail — the PRICES drive the staged stop whatever the rung sizes are, which is what makes 0/0/100 a ratcheting hold rather than an unprotected one.

params.name: exec_tp3_pct
params.label: TP3 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the TP3 limit banks. TP3 is ALWAYS fib 0.000 — the leg's own extreme, the level the External Fib labels TP3 — and at the 0.786 entry it is ~3.67R. ⚠ DEFAULT 100 SINCE 2026-08-07 (was 20), so there is NO RUNNER: the whole position exits at TP3 or at the ratcheting stop. That measured best on every axis — +137.7R vs +90.8R for 30/30/20 and +113.4R for a pure runner, at the SAME drawdown (6.7R), a higher t-stat (5.54) and LESS concentration in the top few winners (9% vs 15%). ⚠ Whatever you leave under 100 becomes the runner again. Only the two rungs BELOW TP3 move with entry depth: a deep entry ladders 0.500 → 0.382.

params.name: bos_tp3_measured
params.label: TP3 = measured move
params.desc: Replaces TP3 with the classic continuation target: the break leg's own range projected forward from the level it broke. That sits BEYOND the leg extreme, so it is the expansion target rather than a retrace-completion one. Ignored when it would land at or behind TP2. On a shallow entry this is what CREATES a TP3, since no fib is left for it.

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: The breakeven stop sits this far beyond the entry, so a scratch still covers costs instead of losing a few cents. It is also why TradingView reports zero breakevens — those exits book a tiny profit, so it files them as wins. The trade label counts them honestly.

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the last part of the position is trailed once TP2 is hit. 'Structure (swing)' parks the stop at the last confirmed swing low (longs) / high (shorts) — it breathes with the trend and usually rides further, but the swing lags, so it hands some back at the turn. 'Fixed step' ratchets on the grid set below.

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: ↳ Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Structure method only. The runner stop sits this many ticks beyond the swing it is trailing, so a wick through that swing doesn't clip the trade.

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: Read by TWO settings, so it is never greyed out: the 'Fixed step' trail ratchets on this grid, and the 'One trail step behind' floor below sits this far under the high-water mark. On gold 1 pip = $0.10 of price, so 50 pips = 5.0.

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: What the stop becomes the moment TP2 is hit, before the trail takes over. 'TP1 price' snaps it up to TP1 — tight, and can scratch the runner on the first pullback. 'Breakeven' gives the runner the most room. The trail can still tighten past this floor, never loosen it.

params.name: bos_close_opp_div
params.label: Close an open trade on opposing divergence
params.desc: ON = close the position when a divergence confirms against it, instead of waiting for the stop or target. The reasoning: an opposing divergence says the move is overextended and is building the NEXT shift of structure, which is the worst thing to be holding a continuation trade into. Fires on a CONFIRMED divergence only, never on extreme RSI — an overbought reading is the normal state of a healthy long.
